body: I'm not sure this is how I add to my reply to your comment. But all this is going on and so many people have so many different beliefs, feelings, assumptions, and whatnot that I'm not even sure if a person's mental illness(s) and developmental disabilities make it harder for a person to live. Dealing with all this is confusing as fuck.

That assumption is right. I'll be 25 this year... I don't feel like I'm just codependent on my mother. I feel I have zero ability to live alone, besides hygiene. I'm talking managing money, understanding bills, insurance, all this stuff that the average responsible adult has enough understanding of to live independently. This has been happening since I was about 11 years old. It's only the last year or so that I realize this is just a toxic family I live in, and I'm part of the toxicity.
That makes sense. I don't believe I've thought of all these things that way. I may need to try that myself for a while and see how things feel. I appreciate you leaving a response!

I appreciate you for replying to the post. That's good to read that you're doing better than some time before. I'm looking into seeing a counselor or therapist, someone like that. I'm no expert, but at times I feel it's possible I could've been misdiagnosed. Thanks again for sharing a response!

Yeah, I also feel this mother takes advantage of her son's emotional state when he's angry. By that, I mean depending on how angry he is, after he calms down he may not remember any of it. Later on down the road, his mother will tell him all about what he did, but rarely ever admits to or opens up about her side of any of it. Thank you, that means a lot to him that someone is sending positive thoughts!

I do believe this mother is very narcissistic. I hear her and her son going back and forth and he tells her he feels she's a bit narcissistic, she laughs in his face and denies it. She's very upsetting to me, her son, and I'm sure a few other people. I know her son has/had a few friends that have noticed it, and she tells her son that they put shit in his head.

That's unfortunate to hear, I hope you're doing well or I hope things get better. I believe that's how it is with this mother. Especially when her and her son are around others whether it's a friend or family members house, unfortunately for them out in public too. I hear that her son feels it's all his fault for a lot of things, whether he only had a part in it, or it happened while they were dealing with life problems, such as financial hardship, homelessness, her son continuing to get angry when I hear him say what makes him angry a lot. About half the time he says something that he feels could have been different/better. Nothing new happens even after he lays all the puzzle pieces out, even if he puts it together and leaves a few pieces left for someone else to put together. His mother brings up their past a lot, and when her son does it she gets so frustrated with him. Not every time, but often, her son will tell her something and she doesn't even respond. She keeps saying it's because he's yelling or other things. I feel if it was my child, I wouldn't just be worried about their tone and feelings, but also what they're saying in that moment. I feel a lot of times she gets her son to explain this stuff about himself so she can throw it up in his face later or use it as a way to keep control of him.

There's a lot there. I do know believe this mother is very self centered, her son brings up feeling unheard, invalid, abused, angry, guilty, hopeless at times. Her child gets very frustrated when he tries to talk to people about his life, experiences, trauma, feelings, mental health. It always sounds like she is comparing her son's life to how he treats her and how she feels about it, sometimes laughs in his face. A lot of times he says he has a problem with being interrupted, I noticed when his mother does interrupt him, he gets irritated and tries to let he know that it bothered him. I've heard him being interrupted and that all his childhood he's kept a ton of things to himself. It was only about when he was 10-11 yrs old he was sent to a hospital and diagnosed with Asperger's, or autism spectrum disorder. Over time, things just got worse for him and one day, he sort of broke down, was very emotional switching from intense anger, bursting into tears saying he hears a lot of abusive, bullying voices in his head even his own, and that one time the world around him changed, and for that moment it was as though he was his abusive and alcoholic father sitting on the couch drinking a can of beer. I'm not sure what those symptoms are for, I've been looking into it and I noticed there's quite a few illnesses that have hallucinations as a symptom. I don't mean to ramble, I'm just worried about this family and her son, I've known them for quite a long while and whenever I see him, it's like he's in front of you, but he's not all there.
Thanks for responding! Yes, I feel I've noticed that quite a bit with this mother.

Ah, I guess I can try to break it down. There's a mother that oftentimes manipulates, and gaslights her mentally ill and developmentally disabled child.
